summary.en: Communal and inter-clan violence continues across South Sudan, with armed men killing civilians on the Juba-Bor road, a raid in Yirol West killing dozens, and a cattle raid in the Eastern Lakes region leaving 20 dead. The SSPDF reported neutralizing a SPLA-IO/NAS commander linked to a massacre of 36 people in Khor Gal-tan, while the Upper Nile governor condemned an attack that killed 23 in Ulang County. Political pressure mounts as the president gave Machar a 48‑hour deadline to return and the UN condemned the surge in violence. The multi-donor ResPEct project ended its four-year effort to combat gender-based violence. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Kommunal og interklan-vold fortsetter i Sør-Sudan, med væpnede menn som dreper sivile på Juba-Bor-veien, et raid i Yirol West som dreper dusinvis, og et kvegraid i Eastern Lakes-regionen som etterlater 20 døde. SSPDF rapporterte at de nøytraliserte en SPLA-IO/NAS-kommandør knyttet til et massakre på 36 personer i Khor Gal-tan, mens guvernøren i Upper Nile fordømte et angrep som drepte 23 i Ulang fylke. Det politiske presset øker ettersom presidenten ga Machar en frist på 48 timer for å komme tilbake, og FN fordømte oppgangen i vold. Det flerdonor-finansierte ResPEct-prosjektet avsluttet sin fireårige innsats mot kjønnsbasert vold. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
